body:
Reduces compilation time for the flagship AMIP coupled run, originally written by an LLM and cleaned up by me.

Every `FieldName` is a singleton, so a `FieldNameSet` and its `FieldNameTree` are fully determined by their types. The set operations were written as unrolled closures specialized on each individual name value, so a key set with N values compiled on the order of N^2 method instances. The atmosphere's Jacobian uses a 324-pair key set, which made this the single most expensive phase of model setup.

For current Atmos main, Jacobian construction drops from ~340 s to ~40 s.

### Changes
The new code compares chains directly, because two names of the same depth share a chain type while two different names never share a FieldName type. Most operations are a map or a filter and stay as ordinary UnrolledUtilities code.

`NameChain` and `NamePairChain` are the chain types, and `name_chain` and `field_name` convert between them. The per-name functions have chain versions that replace them: `is_child_chain`, `is_overlapping_chain`, `is_valid_chain` and `chain_in`. A `FieldNameTree` is flattened once by `tree_chain_vector`.

There are four generated functions that need to compare every value against every other and always scale O(N^2). These back the non-generated functions:
- `check_values`: function the constructor calls to reject names that are duplicated, that overlap one another, or that are not in the FieldNameTree
- `is_value_in_set`: backs `in`, `issubset`, `intersect` and `setdiff`
- `unique_and_non_overlapping_values`: backs `matrix_inferred_diagonal_keys` and `summand_names_for_matrix_product`
- `union_values`:  backs `union`, which `intersect` and `setdiff` also use to enumerate candidates

In my attempts to do this without generated functions I got a max of 30% speedup in the Jacobian construction.
title: Compute FieldNameSet operations once per type
